title: Projects
description: Multi-subject projects and world projects: plan, research, build, test, present and reflect, with free, low-cost and advanced versions.

nodes.title: Plan
nodes.description: Choose a goal, list materials, steps and costs.

nodes.title: Research
nodes.description: Find facts from books, people and reliable websites.

nodes.title: Build
nodes.description: Make, grow or cook the project.

nodes.title: Test
nodes.description: Check if it works, measure and record results.

nodes.title: Present
nodes.description: Show and explain your project to others.

nodes.title: Reflect
nodes.description: What went well? What would you change next time?

competencies.title: Has grown a vegetable garden (or container garden)

items.subject: science project
items.title: Watch a bean grow
items.summary: Put a bean in a jar with wet paper and watch the roots and shoot appear!
steps: 🫙 Put damp paper towel around the inside of a jar.
🫘 Push a dry bean between the paper and the glass.
💧 Keep the paper damp.
👀 Look every day. Roots go down, the shoot goes up!
🖍️ Draw it on day 1, 3, 5 and 7.
🌱 Plant it in soil when it has leaves.

hazards: beans are a choking risk for small children
safety.notes: An adult keeps dry beans away from babies and toddlers. Use a plastic cup if glass may break.

advanced.description: Look at root hairs, then grow it on.

substitutions.use: cotton wool, newspaper or an old cloth

items.subject: world project
items.title: Visit Japan: rice balls and cherry blossom
items.summary: Make rice balls, find Japan on a map and learn to say hello in Japanese.
steps: 🍲 Food: with clean hands, shape cooled cooked rice (an adult cooks it) into balls and wrap with a strip of seaweed or leave plain.
🗺️ Geography: find Japan on a map or globe. It is made of many islands in the Pacific Ocean.
📜 History: long ago, people in Japan made beautiful pottery and wrote with brushes. Look at pictures of old castles.
🗣️ Language: say "konnichiwa" (hello) and "arigatou" (thank you).
🏭 Economics: Japan makes cars, trains, robots and electronics, and has many fishing ports.
🌿 Environment: Japan has mountains, forests and cherry trees that blossom pink in spring.
🏘️ Society: many children walk to school in small groups and help clean their classrooms.
🎤 Present: share your map, dish and three facts with your family. What surprised you?

hazards: cooked rice left out can make people ill
safety.notes: An adult cooks the rice and cools it quickly; eat rice balls the same day or chill them. Child shapes only cooled rice.

better.description: Add a seaweed strip and a cucumber filling.

advanced.description: Fold an origami crane and read a picture book.

substitutions.use: any rice cooked a little soft so it sticks
a lettuce leaf

sources.title: Food safety basics
sources.publisher: FoodSafety.gov (US Department of Health and Human Services)

items.adultNote: Present Japan as a modern, diverse country, not only through traditions.

items.subject: science project
items.title: Build a backyard weather station
items.summary: Make a rain gauge, a wind sock and a weather chart, then become a weather reporter.
steps: 📋 Plan: what will you measure? Rain, wind, cloud, temperature.
🫙 Rain gauge: a straight jar with a paper scale.
🎏 Wind sock: a paper or plastic bag tube tied to a stick. Which way does it blow?
☁️ Cloud chart: draw cloud types and tick the one you see.
📅 Record every day for 2 weeks.
📺 Present a weather report to your family.
🤔 Reflect: did your forecasts come true?

safety.notes: Use child scissors. Put the station somewhere easy and safe to reach.

basic.description: Home-made gauge, wind sock and chart.

advanced.description: Compare home readings with an electronic weather station.

substitutions.use: note where the sun rises (east) and sets (west)

items.subject: world project
items.title: Visit Mexico: corn, colour and ancient cities
items.summary: Make a simple bean and corn taco, map Mexico and learn about its ancient and modern cities.
steps: 🍲 Food: warm tortillas with an adult, fill with beans, sweetcorn and tomato. Corn has been grown in Mexico for thousands of years.
🗺️ Geography: find Mexico between the United States and Central America. Mark Mexico City, the deserts in the north and the jungles in the south.
📜 History: learn about the Maya and Aztec peoples who built great cities, and about Mexico today.
🗣️ Language: say "hola" (hello), "gracias" (thank you) and count "uno, dos, tres".
🏭 Economics: Mexico makes cars and machines, grows avocados and corn, and welcomes many tourists.
🌿 Environment: Mexico has deserts with cacti, rainforests with jaguars, and coral reefs.
🏘️ Society: families often share big meals together; find out about a festival and how it is celebrated.
🎤 Present: share your map, dish and three facts with your family. What surprised you?

safety.notes: An adult heats the tortillas and cuts tomatoes. The child fills and rolls.

better.description: Add a fresh tomato salsa (adult chops).

substitutions.use: chapati, flatbread or lettuce leaves
any beans or lentils

items.subject: garden project
items.title: Build a vegetable garden
items.summary: Plan, plant and look after a vegetable garden, in the ground or in containers. Learn biology, maths, money and more.
steps: 📋 Plan: pick 3 vegetables that grow in your climate and season (biology, weather).
🟫 Soil: feel and test it. Is it sandy, clay or loamy? Add compost (soil science).
📐 Measure the space or containers and draw a plan to scale (mathematics).
💰 Budget: list the cost of seeds, compost and tools; stay within the budget (budgeting).
🌱 Sow and plant with spacing from the packet.
💧 Water: work out how much water each plant needs and collect rainwater if you can (water, environment).
📒 Keep a diary: height, weather, pests, harvest weight (responsibility).
🥗 Harvest and cook a healthy meal from your crop (nutrition).
🚜 Research: how do farmers grow food on a large scale? (agriculture)
🎤 Present your garden and reflect on what you would change.

safety.notes: An adult supervises digging tools. Wear gloves, wash hands and harvested food. Children never use pesticides or weedkillers.

basic.description: Basic container version: grow three vegetables in reused containers on a windowsill, balcony or doorstep.

better.description: A small raised bed or row of grow bags.

advanced.description: A full raised-bed garden with rainwater collection.

substitutions.use: containers: buckets, crates, sacks or bottles
seeds from tomatoes, peppers, beans or potato pieces with eyes
a bottle with holes in the lid

items.subject: engineering project
items.title: Bicycle repair workshop
items.summary: Give a tired bike a full check-up: clean, oil, fix a puncture, adjust brakes, and learn the science behind it.
steps: 📋 Plan: inspect the bike and write a job list with an adult.
🔍 Research: how do gears and brakes use forces and friction?
🧽 Clean the frame and chain; oil the chain lightly and wipe off extra.
🛞 Check tyres; repair any puncture.
🛑 Check brake pads and cable with an adult.
📏 Measure the wheel and work out how far one turn goes (circumference = 3.14 x diameter).
💰 Cost the parts you used and compare with a bike shop service price.
✅ Test: an adult does a final safety check and a slow test ride in a safe place.
🎤 Present a before-and-after report.

hazards: pinched fingers in chain and spokes
safety.notes: An adult supervises and checks brakes, wheels and steering before any ride. Wear a helmet for test rides. Keep oil off brake surfaces.

basic.description: Clean, inspect and do a safety check.

better.description: Clean, oil, fix a puncture and adjust brakes.

advanced.description: A fuller service, or volunteer at a community bike workshop.

substitutions.use: turn the bike upside down on a mat, or hang it from a strong branch with a rope (adult sets up)
a small amount of light machine or sewing-machine oil

sources.title: Bicycle safety
sources.publisher: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration

items.subject: world project
items.title: Visit Kenya: savannah, runners and sukuma wiki
items.summary: Cook sukuma wiki (greens), map Kenya's landscapes and learn some Kiswahili.
steps: 🍲 Food: with an adult, cook sukuma wiki: chopped greens (like kale) fried with onion and tomato. It is often eaten with ugali, a maize porridge.
🗺️ Geography: find Kenya in East Africa on the equator. Mark Nairobi, Mount Kenya, Lake Victoria and the Indian Ocean coast.
📜 History: learn about early human fossils found in East Africa, ancient trading towns on the coast, and Kenya's independence in 1963.
🗣️ Language: say "jambo" or "habari" (hello) and "asante" (thank you) in Kiswahili.
🏭 Economics: Kenya grows tea, coffee and flowers, has a big technology and mobile money sector, and welcomes tourists.
🌿 Environment: the savannah has lions, giraffes and elephants; Kenya also has forests, mountains and coral reefs. Learn how parks protect wildlife.
🏘️ Society: Kenya has more than 40 ethnic groups and busy modern cities; find out what a school day is like.
🎤 Present: share your map, dish and three facts with your family. What surprised you?

safety.notes: An adult supervises chopping and frying. Ugali is very hot; let it cool before shaping.

advanced.description: Add beans and make a full plate with a recipe card.

substitutions.use: spinach, cabbage or any leafy greens
polenta, semolina or rice

items.subject: world project
items.title: Visit India: dal, rivers and many languages
items.summary: Cook a lentil dal, map India's rivers and mountains and learn greetings in Hindi.
steps: 🍲 Food: with an adult, cook a simple dal: rinse red lentils, simmer with water, turmeric and salt, then add fried onion, garlic and cumin.
🗺️ Geography: find India in South Asia. Mark the Himalayas, the Ganges river, Delhi, Mumbai and the coasts.
📜 History: research the Indus Valley civilisation, the many empires, and India's independence in 1947.
🗣️ Language: say "namaste" (hello) and "dhanyavaad" (thank you) in Hindi; India has 22 officially recognised languages.
🏭 Economics: India has large farming, software and technology, film, textile and space industries.
🌿 Environment: India has mountains, deserts, rainforests and mangroves; find out about the monsoon and the Bengal tiger.
🏘️ Society: India is home to many religions, foods and festivals; compare a regional dish from the north and the south.
🎤 Present: share your map, dish and three facts with your family. What surprised you?

safety.notes: An adult is present at the hob. Add spices to oil carefully and stand back.

advanced.description: A full thali plate with several small dishes.

substitutions.use: yellow split peas or any lentils (cook longer)
a general curry powder

items.subject: community project
items.title: Run a recycling campaign
items.summary: Measure how much waste your home or class makes, design a campaign, and measure the change.
steps: 📋 Plan: choose your home, class or street (with permission).
⚖️ Measure: weigh or count rubbish bags for one week.
🔍 Research: what can be recycled locally? Ask the council or waste service.
🎨 Build: make posters, labels and a sorting station.
📊 Test: measure again after two weeks. Calculate the percentage change.
🎤 Present results with a chart.
🤔 Reflect: what worked best to change habits?

safety.notes: Wear gloves. Do not handle broken glass, needles or chemicals; tell an adult.

better.description: Weigh waste and make printed labels.

advanced.description: Analyse data in a spreadsheet and share with the community.

substitutions.use: count bags or measure volume with a bucket

items.subject: world project
items.title: Visit Peru: mountains, potatoes and the Andes
items.summary: Cook a potato or quinoa dish, map the Andes and Amazon, and explore Peru's history and economy.
steps: 🍲 Food: with an adult, cook a potato dish or a quinoa salad. Peru has thousands of potato varieties first grown in the Andes.
🗺️ Geography: map Peru on the west coast of South America: the desert coast, the Andes mountains and the Amazon rainforest. Mark Lima and Lake Titicaca.
📜 History: research the Inca Empire, Machu Picchu, Spanish colonisation and independence in 1821.
🗣️ Language: say "hola" and "gracias" in Spanish, and learn that Quechua is also widely spoken; find the Quechua word for hello.
🏭 Economics: Peru exports copper, gold, fish, coffee and fruit; think about how mining affects jobs and the environment.
🌿 Environment: compare three ecosystems: coastal desert, high mountain grassland and rainforest.
🏘️ Society: compare life in a big city like Lima with life in a mountain village.
🎤 Present: share your map, dish and three facts with your family. What surprised you?

safety.notes: Cook with an adult in the home. Drain potatoes and quinoa away from your body.

basic.description: Simple boiled potatoes with a herb dressing.

advanced.description: Compare potato varieties in a taste test.

substitutions.use: rice, couscous or bulgur
a small amount of mild chilli or paprika

items.subject: world project
items.title: Visit Italy: bread, volcanoes and the Roman Empire
items.summary: Make a tomato bread topping, map Italy and its volcanoes, and trace history from Rome to today.
steps: 🍲 Food: with an adult, toast bread and top with chopped tomato, olive oil and basil.
🗺️ Geography: map Italy, the boot-shaped peninsula in southern Europe. Mark Rome, the Alps and the volcanoes Vesuvius and Etna.
📜 History: research the Roman Empire, the Renaissance artists and scientists, and modern Italy.
🗣️ Language: say "ciao" (hello) and "grazie" (thank you).
🏭 Economics: Italy makes machinery, cars, fashion and food products, and has a large tourism industry.
🌿 Environment: learn how volcanoes and earthquakes shape the land, and about Mediterranean plants like olive trees.
🏘️ Society: compare everyday life, school and meal times in Italy with your home.
🎤 Present: share your map, dish and three facts with your family. What surprised you?

safety.notes: An adult supervises the knife and the grill.

substitutions.use: any cooking oil
dried herbs or home-grown herbs

items.subject: engineering project
items.title: Home energy and money audit
items.summary: Measure your home's electricity use, calculate costs and carbon, and propose savings with real numbers.
steps: 📋 Plan: list 10 appliances and how long each is used.
🏷️ Research: read watts from labels (do not open or unplug anything).
🧮 Calculate kWh (watts x hours / 1000) and cost (kWh x price).
🌍 Calculate carbon (kWh x your country's carbon factor).
💡 Test one change for a week, such as LED bulbs or switching off standby, and read the meter before and after if you can.
💰 Calculate yearly savings and the payback time of any purchase (cost / yearly saving).
🎤 Present a report to your family with a chart.
🤔 Reflect on what was hard to measure.

safety.notes: Read labels and meters only. Never open appliances, sockets or the consumer unit.

basic.description: Calculations from labels and the bill.

better.description: Measure real use with a plug-in monitor (adult plugs it in).

advanced.description: Analyse half-hourly data in a spreadsheet.

substitutions.use: the ratings on appliance labels and your own time estimates

items.subject: business project
items.title: Start a mini business
items.summary: Plan, launch and run a small, safe business for a month: seedlings, repairs, crafts or tutoring.
steps: 📋 Plan: choose a product or service and get permission from a parent or carer.
🔍 Research customers and competitors; set a fair price.
💰 Budget: start-up costs, cost per item, price and break-even point (start-up costs / (price - cost per item) = items you must sell).
🛠️ Build: make the product or set up the service.
📈 Test: sell for 4 weeks and track income and spending.
🎤 Present a profit-and-loss summary.
🤔 Reflect: what would you change?

safety.notes: Sell to family, neighbours or school events with an adult aware. Never meet online buyers alone or share personal details. Food selling must follow local rules.

basic.description: A service like tutoring or garden help.

better.description: Make and sell a simple product.

advanced.description: Run a stall at a community market.

substitutions.use: hand-written posters or word of mouth

items.subject: family project
items.title: Cardboard box house
items.summary: Turn a big box into a little house. Who will live in it?
steps: 📦 Find a box with a grown-up.
✏️ Show where the door and window go. The grown-up cuts them.
🖍️ Draw bricks, flowers and a roof.
🧸 Put a toy inside. It is home!
🗣️ Show your family your house.

safety.notes: An adult does all the cutting before or between sessions and removes staples. The child only draws, sticks and plays.

basic.description: A small box house for a toy.

better.description: A big box the child can sit inside, with a paper roof.

advanced.description: Join boxes into a street with curtains and a door that opens.

substitutions.use: crayons, chalk or coloured paper
a sheet over two chairs as a den

check.question: Who does the cutting?
check.explain: Yes! Grown-ups use the scissors. You do the drawing.

check.question: A house has a...
check.explain: Yes! Houses have doors and windows.

items.adultNote: Let the child decide where things go, even if it looks odd. Spread it over a few short sessions. Photograph or draw the finished house to remember it.

items.subject: family project
items.title: My picture diary
items.summary: Draw one picture every day for a week. At the end, you have a story of your week!
steps: 📄 Fold paper to make a little book.
🌙 Before bed, think: what did I do today?
🖍️ Draw one picture of it.
🗣️ Tell a grown-up about it. They write your words.
📖 After seven days, read your diary together!

hazards: crayons can be a choking risk for babies
safety.notes: Keep small crayon pieces away from babies. Nothing else is needed.

basic.description: Loose pages kept together in a pile.

better.description: A folded book tied with string.

advanced.description: Stick in a leaf, ticket or wrapper from the day.

substitutions.use: folded scrap paper or the back of old envelopes
a pencil or a stick of charcoal

check.question: How many days in a week?
check.explain: Yes! A week has seven days.

check.question: In a diary you draw...
check.explain: Yes! A diary shows your own days.

items.adultNote: Write the child's words exactly as they say them. Name the days of the week as you go. Missed a day? Just carry on.
